causes: Old recorder seeding left the hook-only fixture token total at zero. Native addBatch seeding estimated its rows, causing unintended strategy truncation, including rejected historical empty human/tool rows. Restoring that original scalar fixture baseline leaves complete native row traversal, token estimation and all bounds intact. No runtime compression threshold changed.
Object spread in ObservedValueHistory lost JournalDumpSnapshot prototype methods. Forward rows, chronology and close explicitly to the real snapshot.

Old media participant supported only indexed prepareReplacement. Register real HistoryMediaOwnership for both protocols and count committed public rows at actual acknowledgment instead of inspecting the old indexed media argument.
Direct AdmissionFailureRecorder construction mismatched native history. Shared selected-recorder fixture streams seeds, awaits native commits and independently reopens primary and mirror row trees.

Old enqueue rejection and physical native writer failure have different recovery contracts. Preserve the old fault; native compensation rejects the third row at the real candidate tokenizer admission after two successful admissions. Physical-write poisoning diagnostics remain separate, without claiming successful retry after a poisoned writer.

rows.normalization: Selected-backend durable() replaces compressionDurableValueDigest(recorder); fixture failure replaces recorder.failure. No matcher, expected value, scale, or timeout changed.
